section: The Constitution and separation of powers
text:
The Constitution and separation of powers
The US Constitution (1787) splits power between three branches that check each other:








Branch
Who
How they get there




Legislative
Congress: Senate (100) + House of Representatives (435)
Elected: senators for 6 years, representatives for 2


Executive
President
Elected every 4 years, at most two terms


Judicial
Supreme Court (9 justices)
Nominated by the president, confirmed by the Senate, serve for life

Compared with Norway
TODO: your comparison. Some starting points:

Norway is a parliamentary system: the prime minister needs the support of the Storting (169 seats).
Seats are shared by proportional representation, so many parties are in parliament.
The Storting cannot be dissolved early, so elections are every four years.
